add.issue.name: berth run reads the engine's berth.toml settings; explicit flags override and warn (GitHub #29)

edit.description.md:
GitHub issue #29 (self-reported, open on main as of 27b45ac): berth run builds runner.Options from CLI flags alone; the [[engine]] block's keep_comfyui_up, drain_comfyui, drain_post, drain_slots, priority and needs_mib never reach a berth run.

Fix (option 1 from the issue + the option 2 warning): berth run --as <name> loads the matching [[engine]] block (by --as, then --group) from the suite-merged berth.toml as defaults; an explicitly set flag overrides it and prints a notice naming both values, e.g. berth: --keep-comfyui-up overrides berth.toml keep_comfyui_up = false for comfyui. A run with no flags behaves like a gateway start. No config file = no defaults (unchanged); an invalid config fails the run.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #35 (feat/gui-plane-v1). The /gui/ index lists every configured engine in config order with its live state chip; Launch -> Launching... (greyed, live step, tide strip) -> Open; a row the tab launched opens at once when up; Open on an already-live engine goes straight to its UI without a start cycle. No-UI rows show No UI plus the API address. New endpoint GET /gui/state (one guiRow per engine). Wake page keeps its deep-link contract, button relabelled Launch. Proof: full CI block green (build/gofmt/vet/tests/windows cross-build/golangci-lint v2.14.0: 0 issues), three new tests pin the index contract, and a headless-Chromium pass against a temporary gateway with stand-in engine and stand-in daemon (idle, launching, no-UI rows; only console error is Chromium's favicon, same as the shipped wake page). Awaiting review/merge.
add.issue.comment.author: KG694AXHAQDRB6V2JBM7S1S37P

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: PR #36 (fix/run-engine-settings), with "Fixes #29" so the issue closes on merge. berth run now reads the [[engine]] entry matching --as (then --group) through the suite-merged config, applying it as the default for every setting a flag does not set; a run with no flags behaves like a gateway start. An explicitly set flag overrides the entry and prints which value wins over which (the issue's example line, e.g. berth: --keep-comfyui-up overrides berth.toml keep_comfyui_up = false for comfyui), so file and flags can never silently disagree. Missing config = no defaults as before; invalid config fails the run like the daemon and gateway do. Proof: full CI block green incl. golangci-lint v2.14.0; unit tests for applyEngineEntry plus three CLI-level tests; the built binary driven against a throwaway config (contradicting flag prints both notices and still starts fail-open, flag-less run applies the entry silently, unknown engine unchanged). Decision made here: option 1 from the issue plus the option 2 warning, since option 1 alone would have left the wrapper's flag silently winning in the incident case.
